title: Frequency-aware crack segmentation network (FACS-net) and crack topology loss (CT-loss) for thin cracks
what_it_is: Hybrid ResNet50+MiT encoder with a full-resolution CNN stem, and a decoder that splits fused features into low/high-frequency parts by FFT (FPCM) and reweights them with CBAM; plus BCE+edge+soft-CTS loss. Full text read.
why_it_could_help_us: Targets exactly our failure: thin cracks (<=2 px) lost to spectral bias; on CrackVision12K thinnest stratum it beats Hybrid-Segmentor by 0.306 IoU and DeepLabV3+ 'failed to detect most thin cracks'. The FPCM block is a drop-in for the last U-Net++ decoder stage on top of our HRNet stem.
risk_or_reason_against: Gains are in-domain at 256 px resize with strict IoU; authors say it generalises poorly (nnU-Net best on OmniCrack30k cross-domain), so it addresses thin-line recall, not unseen-module recall. Baseline is DeepLabV3+/Hybrid-Segmentor, not U-Net++/HRNet (our stride-preserving baseline may already capture much of this).
code_available: yes (paper says code released; URL not captured)

title: RSF-Conv: Rotation-and-Scale Equivariant Fourier Parameterized Convolution for Retinal Vessel Segmentation
what_it_is: Plug-in replacement for 3x3 convs with Fourier-parameterised filters equivariant to 8 rotations and 4 scales; tested inside U-Net, IterNet, FR-UNet. Full text read (arXiv version).
why_it_could_help_us: In-domain F1 gain over plain U-Net is small (DRIVE +0.27, STARE +1.12, CHASE +1.10 points) but the paper reports a much larger margin out-of-domain (train on one fundus set, test on another), which is our unseen-module recall problem; cracks run at any angle while our training aug is rot90/flip only. Fewer parameters suits 478 cells.
risk_or_reason_against: Equivariant layers cannot reuse ImageNet/HRNet pretrained weights, which carry our gains; out-of-domain table values were not in the extracted text (only the prose claim). Could be tried in the decoder only.

title: Curvi-Tracker: Curvilinear structure segmentation refinement by iterative tracking
what_it_is: Post-hoc refiner: trackers start at skeleton endpoints of a coarse mask; a Direction-Net and Forward-Net (patch CNNs) decide where to step and how wide to paint; double-confirmation backtracking. Full text read.
why_it_could_help_us: Adds missed crack segments, i.e. raises recall/completeness at a 2 px slack on CrackTree200 (same tolerance idea as our relF1@2), on top of U-Net, U-Net++ and clDice models; ~10% average gain on topology metrics; beats an RNGDet++ tracker and morphological closing. Model-agnostic, so it can sit after C2 without retraining it.
risk_or_reason_against: Correctness drops slightly; on roads trackers followed look-alike lines (driveways, railways) - on EL the look-alikes are gridline fingers, busbar edges and scuffs, so false cracks on crack-free cells (our 1.5x guard) is the main risk. Strokes are jagged (rotation artefacts) which may hurt the width guard.

title: Dual-encoder Multi-Scale Refinement network for robust crack segmentation across diverse domains (DMSRCrack)
what_it_is: CNN+light-ViT dual encoder, multi-scale fusion, a Crack Detail Enhancement Module (Sobel edges + predicted thickness map steering a deformable conv on the skip feature) and a boundary refinement head. Full text read.
why_it_could_help_us: One of few crack papers with leave-one-dataset-out tests against U-Net/U-Net++: best held-out IoU on DeepCrack 0.406, Rissbilder 0.354, Crack500 0.301; removing CDEM costs 1.8% recall. The thickness-gated deformable skip alignment is a cheap decoder add-on for thin-crack recall on unseen sources.
risk_or_reason_against: Gains over U-Net++ are small and not seed-tested; U-Net++ wins on the held-out Volker tunnel set (DMSRCrack recall 0.36 there). Strict Dice/IoU only.

title: RPCANet++: Deep Interpretable Robust PCA for Sparse Object Segmentation
what_it_is: Deep-unfolded robust PCA: stages alternate a Background Approximation Module (low-rank) and an Object Extraction Module (sparse), with memory and contrast-prior modules; ~1.4-4.4 M params. Full text read (datasets, defect and vessel sections).
why_it_could_help_us: EL cell background is close to low-rank (periodic fingers, busbars, uniform wafer), cracks are sparse; an explicit background-vs-sparse split could cut false cracks on gridlines and make the crack response less dependent on per-source contrast. Reported SOTA on infrared small targets and DRIVE/CHASE/STARE vessels.
risk_or_reason_against: Binary only; on NEU-Seg defects it is at U-Net level (IoU 80.3 vs U-Net 79.3, EDRNet 80.5), so gains over a strong U-Net are not shown for larger structures; vessel table numbers were truncated in what I read. Would need to be an auxiliary crack branch next to the 24-class head.

title: Bridging the Geometry Mismatch: Frequency-Aware Anisotropic Serialization for Thin-Structure SSMs (FGOS-Net)
what_it_is: Mamba segmenter that splits features into a low-frequency 'topology carrier' and directional high-frequency bands, then scans along the structure direction instead of raster order. Full text read (setup, results, cross-domain).
why_it_could_help_us: Beats SCSegamba on DeepCrack (mIoU 91.3 vs 90.7, clDice 97.1 vs 94.5), CrackMap (clDice 92.5 vs 59.9) and the 8-material TUT set; applied unchanged to CHASE vessels and Massachusetts roads, clDice +6.05 / +7.46 over SCSegamba.
risk_or_reason_against: No U-Net-type baseline in the tables; 256 px resize; binary task; mIoU averages crack and background. A non-pretrained Mamba backbone would discard our HRNet pretraining.

title: Local shape descriptors for neuron segmentation
what_it_is: Auxiliary output that regresses local shape statistics (diameter, elongation, direction) at every pixel next to the main affinity output. Abstract only.
why_it_could_help_us: Cheap extra head on our decoder: predicting local direction and width around cracks gives dense supervision beyond the 0.19% crack pixels; consistent gains across specimens and resolutions in EM. A direction/width target is easy to compute from our crack masks.
risk_or_reason_against: Evidence is 3D EM neurons (thick, densely packed), not 1-2 px lines; our skeleton-recall and inactive-aux-head experience says auxiliary heads can help singles and fail in ensembles.

title: Automatic High Resolution Wire Segmentation and Removal
what_it_is: Two-stage wire segmenter for very large photos: a global pass on a downsampled image finds wire regions, a local full-resolution pass refines thin wires in tiles; new WireSegHR benchmark. Abstract only.
why_it_could_help_us: Wires are the closest natural-image analogue of our cracks (thin, long, sparse). The global-coarse/local-full-res pattern is a resolution-preserving design that keeps compute low; our Track M showed 2x input helps little, but a local high-res refinement only on candidate regions is different.
risk_or_reason_against: Our cells are only 512 px, so the 'high resolution' problem is smaller; abstract gives no numbers vs a U-Net baseline.

title: A topology-aware segment anything model for domain-invariant crack segmentation (TopoSAM)
what_it_is: SAM encoder plus a serpentine-conv topology branch; trained with 'background adversarial twin learning': pairs with the same crack pasted on different backgrounds. Abstract only.
why_it_could_help_us: The twin-sample idea maps to unseen-module recall: synthesise the same crack on cells from other sources / half-cut layouts and force identical predictions. Reported best generalisation over seven public crack sets.
risk_or_reason_against: SAM backbone was not our winner (DINOv3/SAM-type encoders did not beat HRNet); crack copy-paste and synthetic half-cuts already tried without a confirmed gain; no numbers in abstract.

title: CaPro: Curvilinear-aware Prompt Learning with Single Unlabeled Image for Cost-effective Curvilinear Structure Segmentation
what_it_is: Fine-tuning-free SAM adaptation from one unlabelled image: synthetic curves are Fourier-style-transferred into that image's domain, an oriented sub-curve detector is trained on them, and its filtered boxes become SAM prompts. Abstract only.
why_it_could_help_us: A route to a new, never-labelled module source (the zero-shot set we now need): adapt to its appearance from a single cell without labels. Tested on medical curvilinear and crack sets.
risk_or_reason_against: Binary, prompt-based; unlikely to beat a supervised 24-class model in-domain; no numbers in abstract.

title: Context- and refinement-driven convolutional architecture for robust crack segmentation under real-world and zero-shot conditions (CrackRefineNet)
what_it_is: ConvNeXt backbone with context-aware early injection, adaptive refinement and selective aggregation of intermediate predictions. Abstract only.
why_it_could_help_us: Reports zero-shot testing on unseen sets (F1 42.9%) and up to +3.5% IoU in-domain on RCFD, Crack500, CFD; deep-supervision aggregation of side predictions is cheap.
risk_or_reason_against: Gains are a few points over crack nets, not over U-Net++; zero-shot F1 is low in absolute terms.

title: Seeing cracks in frequency: FD-Mamba accurately segments cracks via frequency-difference priors
what_it_is: Mamba crack segmenter with DWT frequency-difference priors injected into the scans and an FFT-based gated noise-suppression module. Abstract only.
why_it_could_help_us: Frequency priors for thin cracks under textured backgrounds; same mechanism family as FACS-Net, with a background-noise gate that could reduce false cracks on scuffs.
risk_or_reason_against: Three crack datasets, no cross-domain test, no numbers in abstract.

title: Affinity Feature Strengthening for Accurate, Complete and Robust Vessel Segmentation (AFN)
what_it_is: Computes a multiscale affinity field from the predicted mask and uses it to reweight features (contrast-insensitive geometry). Abstract only.
why_it_could_help_us: Claims robustness to contrast changes on XCAD, portal vein, DSA and DRIVE; our five sources differ mainly in contrast. Same group as LIOT (P033).
risk_or_reason_against: Mask-dependent feedback may amplify errors on low-recall unseen cells; affinity heads already in MASTER (TMAL P072).

title: Benchmarking Retinal Blood Vessel Segmentation Models for Cross-Dataset and Cross-Disease Generalization
what_it_is: Trains five published vessel models on the large FIVES set across losses, image quality and disease shift. Abstract only.
why_it_could_help_us: Evidence for the reading in our thesis: given enough data, plain U-Net matches advanced vessel architectures and image quality dominates; argues to spend effort on data/quality, not decoders.
risk_or_reason_against: Not a method; supports not adopting vessel-specific architectures.

title: A new baseline for edge detection: Make encoder-decoder great again (NBED)
what_it_is: Bilateral encoder separating spatial and semantic branches; cascaded decoder where only the spatial features, refined by semantic ones, produce the edge map. ODS 0.838 on BSDS500; also applied to retinal vessels. Abstract only.
why_it_could_help_us: Same principle as our HRNet finding (keep a high-res spatial stream, use semantics only to gate it); could inform a crack-specific spatial head on the HRNet stride-2/4 features.
risk_or_reason_against: Edge benchmarks use 1 px tolerance-matched ODS on natural images; vessel result not quantified in abstract.

title: YoloCurvSeg: You only label one noisy skeleton for vessel-style curvilinear structure segmentation
what_it_is: Inpaints the labelled skeleton out to get clean backgrounds, draws synthetic curves (space colonisation), blends them in with a contrastive synthesiser, trains on the synthetic set. Abstract only.
why_it_could_help_us: >97% of full supervision from one noisy skeleton on OCTA500, CORN, DRIVE, CHASE; a way to make labelled cracks on unlabelled cells of a new source or on half-cut layouts.
risk_or_reason_against: Our crack copy-paste and synthetic half-cuts did not give confirmed gains; EL cracks have specific dark-line profiles that curve generators may not mimic.

title: Unmixing Convolutional Features for Crisp Edge Detection (CATS)
what_it_is: Tracing loss that unmixes side-output features plus a context-aware fusion block; plugs into RCF/BDCN. Abstract only.
why_it_could_help_us: Improves ODS without NMS by 12% (RCF) and 6% (BDCN) on BSDS500: crisper, thinner responses could keep our crack width ratio in the 0.85-1.15 guard while raising precision.
risk_or_reason_against: Crispness matters less under a 2 px tolerance; MASTER already has crisp-edge items (P001 GLR, P008 MatchED).

title: Towards Satellite Image Road Graph Extraction: A Global-Scale Dataset and A Novel Method (SAM-Road++)
what_it_is: SAM-Road successor with node-guided resampling and an 'extended-line' strategy for occlusions; 20x larger global road graph dataset. Abstract only.
why_it_could_help_us: Better generalisation to unseen regions is the headline; the extended-line idea (continue a line through occluded gaps) is analogous to bridging busbar-crossing crack gaps.
risk_or_reason_against: Vector graph output and road scale are far from 24-class pixel masks.

title: SurfSyn: Domain foundation model for pixel-level surface defect detection driven by synthetic data
what_it_is: Foundation model pretrained on 1 M synthetic defect images (steel, pipe, road, wall) with an unsupervised knowledge transfer step; simple mask decoder + detail enhancer. Abstract only.
why_it_could_help_us: Domain-specific pretraining for thin surface defects; the detail-enhancer + synthetic-pretraining recipe could be repeated with synthetic EL cracks for an encoder that transfers across module sources.
risk_or_reason_against: Our MIM/SparK and UCF-EL pretraining did not help; four benchmarks are steel/road, no EL.

title: Crack segmentation network via difference convolution-based encoder and hybrid CNN-Mamba multi-scale attention (DCCM-Net)
what_it_is: Encoder built from six directional/polar pixel-difference convolutions, Mamba+conv skip attention, fusion decoder. Abstract only.
why_it_could_help_us: Pixel-difference convs (PiDiNet idea) encode edge/line gradients explicitly; mIoU 84.9/86.6/80.6 on CrackTree260/DeepCrack/CrackForest.
risk_or_reason_against: In-domain only; mIoU averages background; replaces pretrained encoder.

what_it_is: UDA with a curvilinear-aware discriminator on topological fingerprints, persistent-homology pseudo-label refiner and appearance+topology trust weighting. Abstract only.
why_it_could_help_us: Fits adapting to a new unlabelled module source (our needed new zero-shot set) while keeping crack connectivity.
risk_or_reason_against: Heavy; our Mean Teacher/pseudo-label runs helped only at 5-10% labels; UDA is in D30 scope.
